  title="Agent silent-abort on cold start with high-level task",
  description="""## Symptoms
The agent execution is silently aborted on the very first turn with the error message `[silent-abort] coder returned no tool calls on first turn`. This occurs when the initial task is a high-level feature request (e.g., "implement user logout") without any preceding context-gathering steps.

## Root Cause
The agent's core planning model requires situational awareness of the codebase (file structure, existing patterns, relevant files) to break down a high-level task into concrete tool calls (e.g., `read_file`, `write_file`). When started "cold" with an abstract goal, it lacks the necessary information to formulate a valid, actionable plan, resulting in it producing no tool calls and aborting. The underlying assumption that the agent can autonomously bootstrap its own context from an abstract goal is flawed.

## Fix
The immediate fix is to prepend any implementation plan with a mandatory context-gathering phase. The agent must be explicitly instructed to first list files, identify relevant ones, and read them before attempting to generate implementation code.

## Verification
A subsequent attempt with the same high-level task, but prefaced with instructions to explore the file system, should successfully generate tool calls (e.g., `ls -R`) on the first turn and proceed with the task.

## Prevention
The meta-agent or task dispatcher should be updated to enforce a "context-gathering first" policy for all new software development tasks. Before passing the primary objective to the agent, the system should automatically inject a preliminary instruction set like: "1. List the project's file structure. 2. Identify key files related to the task. 3. Read their contents to understand the current implementation. 4. Then, proceed with the main task."
"""
)
</execute_tool>
